name: Motorcycle
description: A self-propelled vehicle with a seat or saddle and no more than three wheels on the ground, other than a moped: an electric two-wheeler that can go faster than 30 mph is a motorcycle.

restrictions.rule: A seat or saddle, and no more than three wheels on the ground
No power or speed limit; anything faster than a moped's 30 mph lands here however small its motor, since Oregon has no separate motor-driven cycle class
Riders need a driver's license with a motorcycle endorsement, which requires being 16 or older and completing a Team Oregon rider education course
Riders and passengers must wear a DOT motorcycle helmet
Titled and registered with the DMV, with a license plate, and must carry liability and uninsured motorist insurance
Not allowed in bicycle lanes or on bicycle paths, except to cross a bicycle lane when turning or entering or leaving an alley, private road or driveway
One ridden on two wheels off the highway is a Class III all-terrain vehicle there
